title: Replacement of the Fwd Lower Shell Longitudinal Lap Joint by a Machined Integral Splice Strap
abstract: Proposed removal of the built-up forward lower shell lap joint and its replacement by a single machined splice strap that carries the hoop load across a chem-milled step, ending the corrosion and cracking history of the joint on ageing classic aircraft.

sections.reason: The forward lower shell longitudinal joint has now produced three generations of in-service answer and none has closed the problem. Operators of the oldest classic aircraft report corrosion under the fastener heads followed by cracking from the same holes, and two of the three aircraft in the originating request already carry life-limited engineering repairs in the affected bay. Across the tracked population of 340 aircraft delivered before 2002, sixty-one findings have been recorded since 2019 and nineteen of those exceeded the allowable damage limits. The root cause is the built-up joint itself: two thin sheets in contact, drained onto by the cargo compartment, with a fastener row carrying the full hoop load in bearing.
sections.description: The lap joint between stations 1080 and 1360 is cut out on both sides and replaced by a single machined splice strap that carries the hoop load across a chem-milled step, so that the two skin sheets no longer overlap. The vendor strap MOD50333-97 is used as the interim doubler during the cut-out and is then removed. The new joint uses the inboard fitting D5321120539448 at each frame crossing, a re-profiled aft splice plate ORV288354-46, and rivets AES645587-2A in a two-row staggered pattern. All new faying surfaces receive the chromate-free surface protection introduced for metallic fuselage joints, using the surface treatment strap kit D5120112339055 as the process reference article. Access is from outside on jacks with internal support from zones 113, 115 and 121; the cargo lining and floor panels are removed for the full bay length. The forward cargo compartment wiring route crosses the strap footprint at station 1240 and its support brackets must be relocated. Revised detail is on drawings D53211223480, D53211263552 and D51201131570.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 11.4 kg per aircraft, symmetric about the centre line, with a centre-of-gravity shift below 0.06 per cent MAC. No electrical load change. The modification is not interchangeable in either direction: the original skin material is removed and cannot be restored, and the strap cannot be fitted over an existing external doubler. All corrosion-prevention and control tasks and the repeat eddy current inspection of the outer fastener row would be deleted for the modified bay, subject to a new fatigue and damage tolerance substantiation. AMM, IPC, SRM and WDM content for ATA 53-21 and 92-21 will require re-issue, and at least one published repair scheme becomes invalid.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is eleven days on jacks inside a scheduled structural check, on the assumption that the cargo compartments are already open. No production cut-in is proposed; the affected build standard left the line in 2003.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the chromate-free protection process is available for in-service embodiment or only on the production line, whether aircraft carrying an approved external doubler repair in the bay can be modified at all, how the forward cargo compartment wiring route is re-supported across the new strap, and whether the earlier bonded strap standard must be removed first or can be cut out as part of the same operation.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.06 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the affected build standard is out of production
